subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Japan Enters the Race
description: One-minute skill: Japan Enters the Race.

hook.text: In the 1960s, Americans laughed at Japanese cars. They were tiny, tinny, and underpowered.

buildup.text: Brands like Toyota and Datsun sold cheap econoboxes that rusted quickly but cost almost nothing.

discovery.text: Japanese makers studied their flaws obsessively. Each new model was measurably better than the last.

twist.text: When the 1973 oil crisis made gas expensive, suddenly small fuel-sippers were exactly what people wanted.

climax.text: By 1980, Japan exported more cars than any country on earth. Detroit was in a full-blown panic.

punchline.text: The cars Detroit mocked ended up eating its lunch.

quiz.question: What event helped Japanese cars gain popularity in the US?
